subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — SSO/KMS/logging requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechco.com>, Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment follow-up — SSO/KMS/logging requirements

Hi Sam / Jenna —

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation and appreciate you walking us through the architecture and compliance needs. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC / on-prem).

Summary of what I heard:
- SSO: Okta SAML 2.0 required for all internal users, and SCIM for group sync would be preferred.
- KMS/HSM: You need customer-managed keys (CMK) in AWS KMS; legal mentioned CloudHSM-backed key material for key custody.
- Logging & retention: Audit/log retention needs to be 7 years; logs must be exportable to an S3 bucket in eu-west-1 for internal archiving.
- Data residency: Core production traffic will remain in us-west-2 but audit logs must be stored in eu-west-1.

What this typically means (high level):
- Hosted API: fast to start but limited for customer-managed HSM requirements and strict retention/export controls.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity in our environment with customer KMS integration (BYOK) is usually workable; may require custom work for CloudHSM-backed keys depending on exact custody model.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): best fit when CloudHSM-backed key material or strict network isolation is a hard requirement.

Can you confirm the following so we can scope the next steps:
1) Is CloudHSM-backed key material a strict must (i.e., legal requires HSM custody of key material), or would AWS KMS with BYOK (CMK created in your account) suffice?
2) Who owns the KMS account/ARN (security infra contact)?
3) For SSO: do you have a SCIM endpoint or do you need us to support manual group sync?
4) Are there any additional compliance controls (e.g., PCI, specific encryption certs) beyond SOC 2 / ISO that we should map?

Next steps I propose:
- Share your security questionnaire (if you have one) — I can circulate to our security team and map controls.
- Schedule a short call with our infra/security engineering (Rishi) and product (Neha) next week to go over KMS integration options and the logging/export plan.

I attached a short PDF that outlines deployment tradeoffs and typical integration patterns. If we confirm HSM is mandatory we should plan for a Private deployment discussion.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: redwood_deployment_options.pdf

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment follow-up — SSO/KMS/logging requirements

Thanks Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. Answers inline and a couple more details from our side:

1) CloudHSM-backed key material: legal is leaning toward HSM custody for root/key material. They indicated that certain keys that encrypt transaction metadata must have HSM-backed protection. I'll confirm the exact language but treat this as likely required.
2) KMS account: security infra team owns the AWS account and will provide the KMS ARN. I'll introduce our infra owner in the next email.
3) SCIM: we have SCIM for the majority of groups but the PM team uses a separate identity silo; we'd prefer SCIM where possible and can do a one-time manual sync for the smaller group if needed.
4) Additional controls: PCI S1 (payments team) may apply to a subset of requests; we need to flag that.

Preferences:
- For speed to production we prefer to start on Dedicated reserved capacity with BYOK (AWS KMS) if Redwood can support an interim approach for HSM-backed keys (e.g., a design where root key custody is handled in our account and validated by legal). If legal requires customer key material never to leave CloudHSM-managed hardware, we understand Private may be required for full compliance.

I've attached our security questionnaire and will loop in Aaron (infra) and Priya (legal) on the next thread. Also available for a 30m call with Rishi / Neha next week.

Sam
Head of Security, FinTechCo
sam.patel@fintechco.com

Attachments: FinTechCo_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechco.com>, Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment follow-up — SSO/KMS/logging requirements

Sam — perfect, thanks for the context and for attaching the questionnaire. That helps a lot.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- Neha will confirm SCIM / SSO integration options and gaps for the PM silo.
- Rishi will run a technical feasibility check on CloudHSM-backed keys vs BYOK flows and outline what would push us to Private deployment.
- Let's schedule a 30m call with Aaron (your infra) + Priya (legal) and our Rishi/Neha — I proposed Wed 2026-03-09 at 10:00am PT on the calendar (link below).

For transparency, our recommendation path today is:
1) Start with Dedicated reserved capacity + BYOK (AWS KMS) to unblock product and integrate SCIM/SSO.
2) If legal requires HSM custody of specific key material that cannot be accommodated via KMS/BYOK controls, move to Private VPC deployment where we can ensure key material stays in your HSM boundary and provide the required proof artifacts.

I've attached a short doc that lays out the SSO + KMS options and the typical implementation timelines for each path. Please review and let me know if Wed 3/9 10am PT works.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood_sso_kms_options.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Deployment follow-up — SSO/KMS/logging requirements

Looping you both in — thread below from FinTechCo with their questionnaire attached. Quick internal notes:

- They appear to require SCIM + Okta SAML. Neha: can you validate our SCIM mapping + any PM-silo workarounds (manual sync cadence) and estimate effort (S, M, L)?
- They have an explicit CloudHSM ask for some key material. Rishi: please evaluate whether we can meet legal's HSM custody requirement via: (A) BYOK (customer-owned CMK in their AWS account) + attestation, (B) cross-account CloudHSM bridging, or (C) whether this is a hard requirement that pushes to Private deployment. Provide ETA and engineering scope for each option.
- Logging/export: they require export to S3 in eu-west-1 and 7-year retention — confirm our log export pipeline and retention policies; note any egress or cross-region caveats.

Proposed internal next steps:
1) Rishi and Neha to prep 15–30m of notes for the FinTechCo call on 2026-03-09.
2) If Rishi flags HSM custody as non-negotiable, we should prepare a Private deployment presales brief (impact on TAT / cost).

Thanks — this is a good opportunity but will need careful scoping on the KMS/HSM side.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
